Leiden Resolution Sweep for a GO-Term Network

Source: R/network_diagnostics.R
plot_leiden_sweep.Rd

Re-clusters a network across a range of Leiden resolutions, with several seeds at each, to help choose leiden_resolution. Three metrics are plotted against resolution:

Clusters

Number of Leiden clusters (mean and range across seeds).

Modularity

Standard (resolution 1) weighted modularity of the partition: how well separated the clusters are (mean and range).

Stability (ARI)

Mean adjusted Rand index between every pair of seeds. Values near 1 mean the partition does not depend on the seed.

A practical choice is a resolution on a plateau where the cluster count is steady and stability is high. The resolution used for net_result is marked with a dashed line. These metrics describe how robust the clustering is for this one graph; they do not show that the clusters are biologically distinct, because the graph itself depends on GO annotations, DEG cutoffs and overlap_threshold.

Usage

plot_leiden_sweep(
  net_result,
  resolutions = seq(0.2, 3, by = 0.2),
  n_seeds = 10,
  objective_function = NULL,
  seed = 1234,
  title = "Leiden resolution sweep"
)

Arguments

net_result

One network result from run_comparison_networks or generate_overlap_network, or an igraph network.

resolutions

Numeric vector of resolutions to test. Default seq(0.2, 3, by = 0.2), suited to the modularity objective; use much smaller values for "CPM".

n_seeds

Integer. Seeds per resolution (at least 2). Default 10.

objective_function

Character, "modularity" or "CPM". If NULL (default), the objective stored in net_result is used, or "modularity" for a bare igraph network.

seed

Integer. First seed; seeds seed, seed + 1, ... are used. Default 1234.

title

Character plot title. Default "Leiden resolution sweep".

Value

A ggplot object. The sweep results are in its data element (columns resolution, metric, mean, lo, hi).
